newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's Intra Investment increases capital.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's Intra Investment increases capital.

text.p: Lebanon's Intra Investment Co., heir to a financial empire that crashed in the 1960s, increased its capital to 280 billion Lebanese pounds ($180.9 milion) from 280 million, Intra said in a statement on Wednesday.
The statement published by Beirut newspapers said the decision was taken by a shareholders' meeting on Tuesday which also approved the recent revaluation of Intra's fixed assets.

"The company's capital was increased to 280 billion Lebanese pounds from 280 million pounds by adding to capital the sum of 279,720,000,000 pounds from the reserves resulting from the urgent improvement on the fixed assets," Intra said.
Chairman Mahfouz Skayne said last July that Intra's assets were revalued at $200 million.
The Intra statement said the nominal value of each of Intra's shares was raised to 25,000 pounds from 25 pounds.
Intra's shareholders are the Kuwait and Qatar governments and private investors (44 percent), the Lebanese government and central bank (47 percent) and Lebanese private investors.
The statement said the central bank, the Bank of Lebanon, is willing to buy the shares of small shareholders at a price of 25,000 pounds per share throughout the current year.
Intra has a majority holding in Casino du Liban, once the gambling and entertainment centre of the Middle East, which reopened in December after a 20-year shutdown caused by the 1975-90 civil war.
It also owns five Lebanese and French real estate companies and other subsidiaries.
Intra was a major shareholder in Lebanon's Middle East Airlines before the central bank took up most of the national carrier's shares in a debt for equity swap last year.
